claims.claim: Apollinaris the Younger was bishop of Laodicea in Syria and lived approximately from 310 to 390 CE, dying around 382 CE.
He is best known as a prominent opponent of Arianism and as the originator of the Christological view later called Apollinarism.
In the fourth century he wrote a biblical commentary on the Pauline Epistle to the Romans, known today as the "Fragments on the Letter to the Romans" (Fragmenta in epistulam ad Romanos).
The original commentary has been lost; only short excerpts survive in the catenae (chains of patristic commentary) on the Pauline Epistles.
Additional fragments are preserved in the polemical writings of fifth‑ and sixth‑century authors who cited Apollinaris to refute his Christology.
